messages.content: Hello Nora! I'd love to get to know you a little before your stay at Golden Well / U Zlate Studne, so the team can think about the details that matter to you. This chat is optional; you can skip a question or finish whenever you like. What brings you here this time?
Ben and I are celebrating eight years together, and it's our first time in Prague.
Eight years together and a first visit to Prague make this a special trip. What are you most looking forward to discovering together, and have you already made any plans?
Nothing booked. We want one nice dinner and slow wandering. I love architecture and old staircases; Ben likes jazz and little bookshops.

Slow wandering sounds like a lovely way to meet Prague, with plenty to catch both your eyes and Ben’s. For your dinner, what kinds of food or flavours do you both enjoy—and what do you like to drink with it?
We both like fish, roast vegetables and lemon desserts. I usually drink sparkling water; Ben sometimes has red wine. Nothing too drawn-out or formal.

Fish, roast vegetables and lemon desserts sound like a lovely fit for an unhurried dinner; I’ll keep Nora’s sparkling water and Ben’s occasional red wine distinct. Do either of you have any food allergies or dietary restrictions the restaurant should know about?
Neither of us has allergies or dietary restrictions.

Good to know neither of you has any restrictions. After a slow day of wandering, do you tend to reach for a favourite sweet or savoury treat—or is there a particular snack you’d both enjoy finding in your room?
I love dried apricots; Ben loves dark chocolate. Different stashes!
Different stashes—excellent diplomacy. Is there anything about your usual sleep setup or a small bedtime habit from home that makes a real difference when you’re away?
We share a bed but definitely prefer two duvets—I'm always warm and Ben is always cold! Firm pillow for me, soft for Ben. He likes to read before breakfast.

Two duvets and different pillows sound like a sensible truce—and Ben’s pre-breakfast reading is a lovely morning detail. What do mornings usually look like for you both: is there a coffee or tea ritual, or anything else you like to ease into the day?
A cappuccino for me and Earl Grey without milk for Ben. I do ten minutes of yoga. We like breakfast after nine and definitely don't want early tours.

A cappuccino after yoga and a slow breakfast sounds like a lovely start. For your anniversary, would you enjoy a small personal touch—perhaps a note or a playful nod to your eight years—or would you rather keep it low-key?
A small private nod would be lovely. We met sheltering from the rain outside a bookshop. We always say we're still taking the scenic route together. No public announcements or staged romance though.

The bookshop-in-the-rain story and “still taking the scenic route together” make a lovely private reference; I’ll keep the no-public-announcements, no-staged-romance boundary in mind. Are there any scents or flowers you especially like—or prefer to avoid—for a subtle anniversary detail?
No added room fragrance, please. I love irises but not a strong floral smell. Ben doesn't have a favourite flower.

We’ll keep the room free of added fragrance; irises without a strong floral scent sound more your style, and Ben has no favourite flower. As you explore Prague, would you enjoy a few tailored suggestions from the team, or prefer to find things yourselves?
We enjoy warm, informal chats and people's own recommendations. Just not someone checking on us constantly. We like wandering on our own.

That sounds like a lovely balance: friendly local tips when you want them, and room to wander without check-ins. For those architecture-and-bookshop meanders, what does a comfortable walking pace and a good break look like for you both?
Unhurried, with café and bookshop stops whenever something catches our eye. We don't need a schedule or a group tour.

Unhurried wandering with café and bookshop stops sounds just right—and no schedule or group tour. Before we leave it there, is there anything else you’d like the team to know, or anything I’ve got wrong?
Nothing else, thank you.
Thank you, Nora. Wishing you and Ben a lovely first visit to Prague—and a happy anniversary, with plenty of scenic-route moments.

briefs.text:
A) BASIC INFO

Nora and Ben; two guests, 20–23 November 2026. First visit to Prague and celebration of eight years together. They have no plans booked and hope for one nice dinner and unhurried independent wandering.

B) COORDINATION

Reception is the assigned handoff and should coordinate with housekeeping and the restaurant as needed. Dedicated concierge availability is unconfirmed. Hotel information is based on public material checked 5 October 2026; operational details, availability and proposed arrangements are not confirmed.

Key checks: whether the room can provide two separate duvets and Nora’s firm/Ben’s soft pillow preferences; no added room fragrance; morning drink and breakfast service options after 09:00; and whether the restaurant can offer a shorter, less formal seasonal dinner with a new quote. No early tours or constant check-ins.

C) GUEST PROFILE

Nora loves architecture and old staircases; Ben likes jazz and small bookshops. Together they enjoy slow wandering, stopping at cafés and bookshops when something catches their eye, without a schedule or group tour. They welcome warm, informal conversation and staff recommendations, but prefer to explore independently without frequent check-ins.

They both like fish, roast vegetables and lemon desserts. Nora usually drinks sparkling water; Ben sometimes has red wine. Neither has allergies or dietary restrictions. They prefer dinner that is not too drawn-out or formal.

Nora loves dried apricots; Ben loves dark chocolate, and they prefer separate stashes. They share a bed but want two duvets: Nora is usually warm and prefers a firm pillow; Ben is usually cold and prefers a soft pillow. Nora does ten minutes of yoga and likes a morning cappuccino. Ben likes Earl Grey without milk and to read before breakfast. They both prefer breakfast after 09:00.

They welcome a small, private anniversary nod inspired by meeting while sheltering from rain outside a bookshop and their phrase “still taking the scenic route together.” No public announcements or staged romance. Nora likes irises but not a strong floral smell, and requests no added room fragrance. Ben has no favourite flower.

Experience suggestions: see F.

D) RECEPTION

Offer friendly, informal recommendations when useful, without scheduled check-ins. Keep any Prague suggestions self-guided and flexible; do not steer them toward an early start, group tour or fixed itinerary.

For mornings, preserve the separate preferences: Nora’s yoga and cappuccino; Ben’s tea and reading before breakfast; breakfast after 09:00. Confirm available drinks and service timing rather than assuming a particular service or delivery.

E) ROOM PREPARATION

Reception to ask housekeeping to check whether the assigned room can be set with two separate duvets and a firm pillow for Nora and soft pillow for Ben. The published bedding menu does not confirm these exact options or availability. Do not add room fragrance.

Consider, subject to hotel approval and relevant stock/fee checks, placing separate dried-apricot and dark-chocolate options for Nora and Ben. These are distinct preferences, not a request or a confirmed minibar offering; reception should check with the appropriate food/service team before arranging anything.

F) CONCIERGE — EXPERIENCE SUPPORT

• Dinner proposal — The restaurant’s published menu demonstrates fish, vegetable and dessert expertise, but does not establish a shorter menu or guarantee particular dishes. Ask the restaurant whether it can offer a concise, less formal seasonal dinner shaped around their interest in fish, roast vegetables and lemon desserts. Confirm feasibility, current dishes, service pace, availability and a new price before presenting it. Keep Nora’s sparkling water and Ben’s possible red wine distinct; confirm current choices. The published full tasting menu is not the lead proposal for their stated preference.

• Independent Prague recommendations — Reception, or a concierge if one is confirmed, to have warm, date-relevant suggestions ready for architecture and old staircases, small bookshops, cafés and jazz during 20–23 November. Verify current details, especially live jazz listings, and offer recommendations without turning them into a schedule or booking. If the hotel cannot verify suitable options internally, reception should undertake focused research for those dates.

• Private anniversary detail — Consider a discreet, hotel-authored card placed privately in the room, subject to hotel approval. It could use the shared phrase “still taking the scenic route together” and a small illustrated iris as a quiet reference to their story and Nora’s flower preference. This avoids added room fragrance and does not assume a floral arrangement, public recognition or staged display. Coordinate placement with housekeeping; do not represent the card or any other attention as included or already arranged.
